reference_items.native_verdict: Playable; two named gaps and one unmeasurable check

checks.observed: 30 identical casts produced one distinct damage value (53); stdev 0.000000. The determinism guard reports 0 violations before and after every cast at all five classes.
no cast i-frames observed on any frame of any run; the five denied buttons during levitation are refused at the input gate rather than after the move starts.

checks.not_run_reason: MagicSystem.hitboxRecords() emits per-projectile turn_rate_dps and travel_f, but engine.getHitGeometry() does not include it and no other harness surface exposes a projectile's heading. The checkpoint's headline figure (60.00 deg/s before the cutoff at travel_f 53, 0.000 after) therefore cannot be reproduced by a critic. Unmeasurable, recorded as such.

checks.observed: a projectile fired on the release heading hit a body standing 15 deg off axis at 14 m (53 damage) and missed one at 30 deg. Within the 20 deg acquisition cone the player does not have to aim. Round 1 recorded 0.000 deg/s and passed AR-1 A7 on 'no player homing exists'; that sentence is no longer true.

no can_cast_in_combat gate exists on the cast path. A commissioned LIGHT-class Intervention cast with in_combat true moved the player 44.77 m to a shrine; a LIGHT-class Recall moved 84.74 m from [60,0,60] to the mark. The shipped carriers are RITUAL and are interrupted, but spellmaking sets the class and nothing restricts it.

reference_items.why_not_ten: Frame data, commitment and determinism are still excellent and would carry a 7 alone. Three things stop it: an in-fight teleport reachable through this piece's own spellmaking system against a named S19 prohibition; a new acquisition cone that makes aiming optional inside 20 deg; and a headline ballistics claim that no harness surface lets a critic reproduce.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Gate the teleport effects on out-of-combat (S19/S7), expose hitboxRecords() through getHitGeometry() so AP-M3 is measurable, and either drop the acquisition cone or record the residual-aim-error distribution M4 actually asks for.

0. No non-damage effect takes hp from the target. combat-bridge.js's accumulator is closed over the five-element DAMAGE_EFFECTS set.

Converse: a fire spell took an enemy from 412 hp for 405 damage bare, 5 damage under shield (physical) and 5 damage under resist_element — identical. body.mitigation is one multiplier with no element.

only PARALYSED is read (magic/system.js writes b.state = 'PARALYSED' and the enemy stops: measured PARALYSED for 5 consecutive samples). BURNING procced twice on a live enemy and its state stayed REPOSITION throughout; FROSTBITE, CONCUSSED and POISONED write body.statusProc[kind] and nothing outside statusReport() reads it.

pos[1] 5.5867 m, Focus 124 -> 98.62 over the climb (1.5/m), drift 1.388 m/s against a 1.4 cap and a measured walk of 3.173 m/s, state AIRBORNE, light/heavy/block/roll/parry all dropped with state and move unchanged, iframe false on 60/60 frames, and a 37-damage hit landed in full and ended the flight. reference_items.why_not_ten: The generic applicator is genuinely dead and levitation is genuinely built. But 55 code paths produce 33 outcomes a player could tell apart, four mitigation effects are literally one number, four of five status procs are written and never read, and eight effects act on registers that exist only inside game/src/sim/magic/**.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Give body.mitigation a per-element channel and make resist_element/resist_disease/shield read different ones; make the four non-paralysis procs change something (a damage-over-time, a stagger threshold, a speed multiplier); and connect telekinesis/detect_*/mend_item/buoyancy/breathe_water to the interaction, render, durability and traversal-water systems that already exist.

reference_items.native_verdict: The arithmetic and the economy are right; the system it gates is frozen and it opens a hole S19 closed

reference_items.why_not_ten: The cost model, the gold line and the enchanting arithmetic are all correct and independently reproduced. The system they price is capped at two effects forever, and the one place spellmaking touches a seam ruling it breaks it.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Feed MagicSystem.skills from sim.progression.skills, and refuse a non-RITUAL class for mark/recall/intervention in quoteSpell().

It is bounded (20 deg cone, stops at the declared cutoff) and the cutoff behaviour is declared by cast-classes.json, so this is recorded as a softening of the aim requirement rather than an AR-1 automatic fail: it is not one of the six mechanics AR-1 enumerates and S26 forbids widening AR-1 to cover ordinary defects. It is charged to RI-MAG01 instead.

a commissioned LIGHT-class Intervention moved the player 44.77 m to a shrine with in_combat true, and a LIGHT-class Recall moved 84.74 m to the mark. AR-2's enumerated leak is 'bonfire warp', and S7/S19 explicitly PERMIT Intervention as part of the travel network out of combat — so this is not the enumerated leak and I do not fail AR-2 on it. It is a direct breach of S19's named prohibition ('no recall out of a fight, no intervention as an escape button') and is charged to RI-MAG01 and RI-MAG03 and named here so the ruling is on the record rather than absorbed.

score.band_label: Between 'Recognisable but wrong' and 'Recognisably attempting the thing' — the catalogue became a set of verbs and the quest machine turned on; the character who casts them cannot get better at it

biggest_gap.what: MagicSystem.skills is a private object initialised to {sorcery:30, root_speech:30, warding:30, veiling:30} that no gameplay path writes. Measured in four shipped states (default, arena_flat, dungeon_primary, helstrom-market): 47 of 72 shipped spells attunable and 25 refused — all 17 tier-3 and all 8 tier-4 — and setAttuned() drops them silently. 40 casts at a live target, a HEARTH rest, H.setSkills() on the character sheet and H.grantSkillUse('cast_effective') all leave the tier-3 attune at 0/1 and quoteSpell().attunable_now false; only H.setMagicSkills(), a harness call with no in-game counterpart, flips it to 1/1 and true. Spellmaking is capped at two effects for the whole game ('3 effects needs skill 50; your best relevant school is 30'). In the other direction, RI-MAG04's magic resolutions gate on sim.progression.skills, which is {} in every shipped state and which the magic system never writes: the coupling between the character's magic skill and the magic system is 0.00 in both directions, with the null control clean (perturbing magic.skills 30->100 does flip the gate, so the probe is driving a live gate and not a stub).
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A mage who plays this game for forty hours casts exactly the spells they could cast in the first minute — a third of the shipped catalogue, every tier-3 and tier-4 spell, and every three-effect spell they might commission are locked behind a number that nothing they do can move, and the quest resolutions magic exists to unlock read a different, empty number.

remedy.action: Make MagicSystem.skills a VIEW of sim.progression.skills rather than a private copy: replace the literal at game/src/sim/magic/system.js:59 with a getter that reads sim.progression.skills (mapping root_speech <-> root-speech, which are spelled differently in the two files today), so _effectiveSkillFor, focusCost, the tier gate and quoteSpell's effect-count all read the character sheet. Then close the loop that fills the sheet: add `skill` to the effect_apply and spell_hit event payloads in game/src/sim/magic/system.js and game/src/sim/combat-bridge.js so game/src/character/skilluse.js:stepSkillUse banks the SPELL'S OWN school instead of hardcoding 'sorcery'; and make setAttuned() emit an `attune_refused` event with the shortfall instead of silently returning a shorter list. Ensure sim.progression.skills is non-empty in the shipped states (engine.js:575 fills it from ch.skills, which is empty when no character has been composed) — coordinate with W1-07, whose census owns that seeding, and record the seam if it cannot be done here.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run tools/harness/critic-w1-14-r2f.mjs, which never calls setMagicSkills(). Required: (a) in every shipped state, the attunable count rises when the character sheet's warding/sorcery rise, and 72/72 are attunable at skill 100; (b) 40 casts of a warding spell at a live target raise sim.progression.skills.warding by a non-zero amount and emit >= 1 skill_use event with skill == 'warding' (not 'sorcery'); (c) a three-effect spell is quotable once any relevant school reaches 50; (d) H.questResolutions('Q-MAG-01') reports the magic resolution available after the skills were reached BY CASTING, with no setSkills or setMagicSkills call anywhere in the probe; (e) setAttuned() on an under-skilled spell emits an attune_refused event naming the shortfall.

secondary_observations.what: MITIGATION IS KIND-BLIND, AND THE BUILDER'S OWN HEADLINE NUMBER IS THE PROOF. body.mitigation is a single multiplier that resolve.js:mitigate() applies to every incoming number regardless of source. Identical scripted PHYSICAL hit of 100: baseline 100, shield 69.12, resist_element 15.00, resist_disease 15.00 — a resist-DISEASE buff blunts a sword by 85%. Converse: a fire spell took 405 hp off a bare enemy, 5 under shield (physical) and 5 under resist_element. The checkpoint reports '100 unbuffed, 53.68 with shield, 30.52 with resist_element' as a success; it is the same measurement.

EIGHT EFFECTS ACT ON REGISTERS NOTHING OUTSIDE game/src/sim/magic/** READS. telekinesis writes M.reachM, but the interaction that actually reaches for a prop tests o.reach_m in engine._censusStep. detect_life/detect_key write M.markers, which no renderer pass and no entity consumes. mend_item writes an item-condition table that exists nowhere else in the build. buoyancy and breathe_water write M.water.{buoyant, breathes, drownF}, while the water the player actually swims and drowns in is engine.traversal (water_band, breath_s, submerged). restore_attribute has no reachable precondition: nothing in the build ever lowers an attribute. cure_disease and cure_poison splice sim.quest.afflictions, which only H.addAffliction() writes — the diseases the game can actually give you are pushed by hazards.js onto sim.player.afflictions, a different array. These are the shapes RI-MTH07 §A calls orphan model and orphan predicate, one layer in from round 1.

FOUR OF THE FIVE STATUS PROCS ARE WRITTEN AND NEVER READ. BURNING procced twice on a live enemy and its state stayed REPOSITION throughout; only PARALYSED is consumed (magic/system.js sets b.state and the enemy stops, measured for 5 consecutive samples). FROSTBITE, CONCUSSED and POISONED set body.statusProc[kind], which nothing outside the expiry deleter and statusReport() reads. This is the UNREAD_TIMER failure moved one level down, below where RI-MAG06's census looks.

THE CENSUS'S DECLARED-VS-MEASURED CHANNEL IS NEARLY VACUOUS. mag-census.mjs records the build's own `declared_consumer` alongside its own reading 'so the two can disagree in public', but it never compares the two consumer strings — the only disagreement it can raise is `self_report_disagrees`, which fires solely when the build says changed:false and the census still classed the row FUNCTIONS_AS_SPECIFIED (6 rows do). Every one of the 36 rows where the declared and measured consumer strings actually differ is a cosmetic wording difference the tool cannot see, and its `consuming_system` field is a hardcoded label from its own PROBES table rather than a measurement. If a handler declared the wrong consumer, this census would not notice.

THE TWO STRUCTURAL BUGS ARE GENUINELY FIXED. The `_emit(frame, kind, fields)` collision is closed: 5 status_buildup and 2 status_proc events arrived on the stream with their own event types, `status_kind` carrying the element, and no event type is ever an element name. The SimState.reset() journal detachment is closed: after a loadState('arena_flat') that would have detached the QuestEngine in round 1, hist_sight wrote getQuestState().journal 0 -> 1 with the prose entry present. Both confirmed independently of the builder's own probes.

getQuestState() STILL DECLARES THERE IS NO QUEST RUNTIME. Its `_declared_incomplete` block reads missing: ['a quest runtime: no quest in this build can be started, advanced or completed by playing'] — which is now false, and which is the single most-read harness surface for the quest area. It also exposes neither `afflictions` nor `travel.mark`, so the consuming systems for cure_* and mark are not readable through the call every critic uses.

THE DEFENSIVE GUARD ON ANOTHER PIECE'S LINE PAPERS OVER NOTHING. engine.js:215 reads `this.sim.censusDriver = (input) => (this._censusStep ? this._censusStep(input) : null)`. `_censusStep` is a prototype method defined at engine.js:964 and is always truthy, so the guard is dead code today — it cannot mask a missing census driver because there is no state in which one is missing. It was added to survive a concurrent commit that had removed the method. Harmless; worth deleting rather than keeping as a permanent apology.

THE DRY WELL DATA STILL CONTRADICTS S27 AND ITS OWN IMPLEMENTATION. engine.hearthRest() correctly implements S27's drawback (focus_restores_at_hearth false for the sign). But game/data/progression/birthsigns.json still declares the power as 'You absorb 55% of the magnitude of any spell effect that lands on you, as Focus' and the drawback detail as 'Focus is refilled only by absorption and by consumables' — which contradicts the hearth-denial the engine now applies, and `spell_absorption` is derived in character/derive.js and consumed by nothing. tools/analysis/magic-audit.mjs still fails on CROSS_ITEM_CONFLICT_birthsign_focus_absorption (10 pass, 1 fail). The checkpoint says this 'needs a RULING'; S27 has ruled, in the same commit, and the data has not been amended to match.

REGRESSIONS ARE GREEN AND I RAN THEM MYSELF: mag-probe 19/19 including AR3_X1 and AR3_X4; save-audit round-trip EQUAL on all four states (manifest-extra 13/1 belongs to W1-15's crime ledger and W1-07's NPC/prop records, not this piece); lint-determinism 0 errors over 87 files; magic-audit 10 pass / 1 fail (the birthsign conflict above).

MY OWN FIRST INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG AND THE BUILD WAS RIGHT. The first run of critic-w1-14-r2a.mjs reported 22 effects as 'moved nothing'. The flattener recorded only each array element's `id`, so a lock going locked:true -> false was invisible; and subtracting the control by key deleted every hp-moving effect because the control's own scripted hit also moved hp. diag-touch.json is the artifact that caught it — the spells were resolving all along. arbitration_questions.question: Does spellmaking inherit a seam ruling's fence, or may a commissioned spell take any cast class? S19 forbids recall out of a fight; the shipped carriers obey it only because they are RITUAL and rituals are interrupted. Nothing states that the fence is the class rather than the effect.
arbitration_questions.souls_side: The cast class is a combat property and the player should be free to buy a faster version of any spell; the fence should be an explicit combat check, not an accident of duration.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: Spellmaking is Morrowind's crown jewel and its whole point is that you may combine anything; the fence must therefore live on the effect, and the teleport effects must be refused a non-ritual class at quote time.

Escalation ladder: the first sample — the builder's own census, re-run at HEAD — returned 55/55 and would have carried a comfortable pass. Rung 2 (change the sample) built an independent instrument and confirmed 55/55, which is the honest answer. Rung 4 (measure the second-order property) is what produced this verdict: not 'does an effect move a system' but 'how many distinguishable outcomes do 55 handlers produce' (33) and 'can the character who casts them ever get better at it' (no). CC-scan: manual. No sentence in this verdict excuses a V* or M* failure with 'it matches Morrowind's look', 'stylised', 'retro' or 'the art direction carries it'.

That gap is closed, and closed properly: I built my own instrument rather than re-running the builder's, and it agrees — 55/55, HP_DAMAGE_ONLY 0, UNREAD_TIMER 0, GENERIC-APPLICATOR 0/55. Levitation, the quest runtime, the control verbs, the two structural bugs, the economy and the VFX renderer are all real work that measures. The piece fails on something the previous round could not see because it was standing behind the thing that was broken: the character who casts these spells cannot get better at casting them, and the register the quest gate reads is not the register the magic system uses.
